candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Slovakia geographical area hub
candidates.why_relevant: Single entry point listing every ECB dataset that carries a Slovakia (SK) reference-area row, including payment statistics, card, ATM/POS and terminal series. Best snowball hub for enumerating SK series keys across the whole ECB statistical estate.
candidates.source_subtype: statistical data portal / country landing page
candidates.legal_status: ECB open data; reuse permitted with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use as a manual/HTML pointer to harvest dataset codes, then pull actual series via the SDMX REST API rather than scraping the SPA.
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payment statistics Slovakia cards POS terminals dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics data category (PSS / payment services, LVPS and retail payment systems)
candidates.why_relevant: Harmonised semi-annual payment statistics collected under Regulation ECB/2020/59, with SK country rows: number of cards, card payments, terminals, credit transfers, direct debits, e-money. Longer-run and more comparable than NBS national tables.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX REST API pull filtered on REF_AREA=SK; store series keys + vintages for revision tracking.
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payment statistics Slovakia cards POS terminals dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payment card accepting devices (ATM / POS terminal counts)
candidates.why_relevant: The single most directly on-topic ECB cut for Printec-type interests: counts of ATMs, POS terminals and e-money card accepting devices per country, including Slovakia — terminal estate size and growth over time.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX API; also keep the deprecated annual PTN/PTT series for pre-2022 back-history.
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payment statistics Slovakia cards POS terminals dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Cards and card payments key figures
candidates.why_relevant: Curated headline indicators (cards per capita, transactions per card, average value) with country comparison views; fast way to benchmark Slovakia against euro-area peers without building series keys.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: CSV export from the indicator page; or resolve underlying series keys and use the API.
queries_used: ECB Data Portal payment statistics Slovakia cards POS terminals dataset

candidates.source_name: ECB Payments statistics press releases (semi-annual, H1/H2)
candidates.why_relevant: Narrative + chart release accompanying each semi-annual payment statistics vintage; gives the official reading of trends (card share, contactless, fraud, terminals) and flags methodological breaks that matter when splicing SK series.

candidates.source_name: ECB SPACE — Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (landing page)
candidates.why_relevant: The flagship Eurosystem consumer payment-diary survey (2020, 2022, 2024 waves) with per-country results including Slovakia: cash share at POS, P2P cash use, stated preferences, cash access perceptions. Only harmonised demand-side cash-usage evidence for SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the main report + annex PDFs each wave; extract the SK country column from country tables.
queries_used: ECB SPACE study 2024 payment attitudes consumers euro area country Slovakia

candidates.source_name: ECB SPACE 2024 — Annex B (country-level statistical annex)
candidates.why_relevant: The annexes carry the machine-extractable per-country tables (SK rows) behind the SPACE headline text — cash/card/mobile shares by transaction value band, location, and payment situation. This is where the usable Slovakia numbers actually live.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PDF table extraction (camelot/pdfplumber) targeting SK columns; version by wave year.
queries_used: ECB SPACE study 2024 payment attitudes consumers euro area country Slovakia

candidates.source_name: ECB SPACE 2020 report (first wave, baseline)
candidates.why_relevant: Baseline wave (2019 diary fieldwork, 17 euro area countries incl. Slovakia) needed to measure the SK cash-to-card shift over time rather than reading a single snapshot.

candidates.source_name: ECB Occasional Paper 201 — The use of cash by households in the euro area
candidates.why_relevant: The pre-SPACE (SUCH 2016) study establishing the long-run cash-usage baseline per country, incl. Slovakia; essential for a 2016→2024 cash decline narrative and for understanding the methodology lineage of SPACE.

candidates.why_relevant: Successor to the ECB card fraud report series; semi-annual fraud data by instrument (cards, credit transfers, cash withdrawals, e-money) with per-country tables covering Slovakia. Directly relevant to ATM/POS fraud and SCA effects.

candidates.source_name: ECB SDMX 2.1 RESTful web service (ECB Data Portal API)
candidates.why_relevant: The machine-readable access layer for every SK payment/card/terminal series above — XML/JSON/CSV, data-discovery endpoints, and bulk download for datasets not exposed in the web UI. This is the recommended collection channel for the whole cell.

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics methodology page
candidates.why_relevant: Explains definitions, breaks in series, derogations and the reporting manual behind the SK rows. Without it, cross-country ATM/POS comparisons are easy to misread (e.g. terminal definitions, MCC breakdowns, resident vs non-resident acquiring).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot on each major regulation/guideline change; store alongside data vintages.
queries_used: ECB payments statistics methodology Regulation ECB/2020/59 reporting national central banks explanatory notes

candidates.source_name: Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 (ECB/2020/59) on payments statistics — EUR-Lex
candidates.why_relevant: The legal instrument that forces Slovak PSPs to report card, terminal and fraud data to NBS and thence to the ECB. Reading the annexes tells you exactly which variables exist for SK before you go looking for them, and is available in Slovak on EUR-Lex.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch of EN + SK language versions via EUR-Lex CELEX (32020R2011); watch for amending acts.
queries_used: ECB payments statistics methodology Regulation ECB/2020/59 reporting national central banks explanatory notes

candidates.source_name: ECB public consultation file on the payments statistics Regulation (FAQ + draft annexes)
candidates.why_relevant: Consultation FAQs and draft annexes reveal the reporting burden debate and the exact variable list (MCC breakdowns, remote/contactless, fraud typologies) — useful for anticipating which SK series will appear and which are derogated.

candidates.why_relevant: Reports per-country shares of instant payment volumes settled in TIPS; the 2024 edition explicitly names Slovakia as one of the three largest contributors of euro instant payments — a high-signal, hard-to-source fact about the SK instant-payments market.

negative_findings.description: The ECB Consumer Expectations Survey (CES) covers ~19,000 consumers in 11 euro area countries (BE, DE, IE, GR, ES, FR, IT, NL, AT, PT, FI). Slovakia is not among them.
negative_findings.result_summary: CES payment-preference and digital-payment modules cannot be used for Slovakia country estimates; SPACE remains the only harmonised ECB consumer-level source with SK coverage.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids a wasted collection pipeline and prevents mistaking euro-area CES aggregates for SK-representative figures.

negative_findings.description: Slovak-language searching of ECB statistical content returned almost nothing on payment/card/ATM statistics: ecb.europa.eu serves only general institutional pages (ECB/ESCB overview, euro overview, banknote circulation) in Slovak.
negative_findings.result_summary: No .sk-language ECB payment-statistics dataset page, SPACE report, or fraud report was found. The Slovak-language layer for this cell is effectively NBS relaying ECB output, plus EUR-Lex Slovak legal texts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell must be collected in English; local-language monitoring should be pointed at nbs.sk and EUR-Lex SK rather than at the ECB site.

negative_findings.description: No ECB-published, Slovakia-specific standalone SPACE country annex (a separate SK-only PDF) was located via search; SK appears as rows/columns inside the euro-area report and its annexes.
negative_findings.result_summary: Slovakia coverage in SPACE is confirmed at country-row level (e.g. 42% cash for P2P), but as part of pooled annex tables rather than a dedicated national report.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be table-extraction from the euro-area annexes; do not budget for a per-country document feed.

negative_findings.description: The ECB payments-statistics press-release index URL and the ECB Data Portal API help URL were inferred from related result URLs rather than returned directly by search, and no page was fetched to confirm them.
negative_findings.result_summary: Individual release URLs (pis2024h1, pis2024h2, pis2025h1) and help pages (getting-data-web-services-sdmx, useful-tips, downloading-data) did appear in results; the index/API-root paths are my inference.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification should resolve these two roots before wiring them into a scheduler.

negative_findings.description: ECB payment statistics moved from annual (ECB/2013/43) to semi-annual with a much wider variable set (ECB/2020/59), and the old annual dataset is explicitly labelled 'discontinued'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two distinct SK datasets exist with a methodological break around 2021/2022; naive concatenation will create false trend jumps in terminal and card counts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any long-run SK ATM/POS or card series must document and flag the break rather than silently splice.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a metadata-discovery pass against the ECB SDMX API (dataflow + DSD for the payments dataflows) and enumerate all SK series keys, storing them as a durable collection manifest.

brief: The ECB/Eurosystem layer is the strongest and most machine-readable source of Slovak payment, card and ATM/POS statistics: the ECB Data Portal carries harmonised SK rows for payment services, card payments and card-accepting devices under Regulation ECB/2020/59, all reachable through a free SDMX 2.1 REST API with bulk download, plus a discontinued annual dataset holding the pre-2022 back-history. On the demand side, the SPACE consumer payment-diary study (2020/2022/2024 waves, with statistical annexes) is the only harmonised evidence on Slovak cash usage and payment preferences, complemented upstream by ECB Occasional Paper 201 and interpretively by SUERF policy briefs from ECB authors. Fraud and infrastructure are covered by the joint EBA-ECB payment fraud reports (successor to the ECB card fraud series, with country tables) and by the TARGET Services Annual Report, which flags Slovakia as one of the three largest contributors to euro instant payments in TIPS. The main practical constraints are that this layer is English-only in substance (Slovak surfaces only via NBS relays, EUR-Lex SK texts and the localised banknote-circulation page), that the 2021/22 annual-to-semi-annual regime change creates a real series break, and that concrete SK SDMX series keys still need to be enumerated before collection.
